disease_label_per_paper: Giant perinephric abscess associated with decompensated cirrhosis
presentation_summary: 67-year-old man with decompensated cirrhosis from hepatitis B and alcohol use presented with 10 days of yellow watery diarrhea, fatigue, poor appetite, and abdominal distention.
On admission he was febrile at 38.6 C, blood pressure 124/75 mmHg, pulse 95/min, respiratory rate 20/min, and oxygen saturation 98%.
Exam showed jaundice, tense abdominal distention, and bilateral lower-limb edema.

Labs showed CRP 59.32 mg/L, procalcitonin 0.63 ng/mL, hemoglobin 11.6 g/dL, WBC approximately 7.93 x 10^9/L with neutrophil predominance, albumin 24.4 g/L, total bilirubin 55.6 umol/L, INR 1.51, D-dimer 7004.4 ng/mL, and platelets 124 x 10^9/L.

Contrast-enhanced CT showed cirrhosis, splenomegaly, massive ascites, and a low-density cystic mass with peripheral rim/septal enhancement in the right posterior perinephric space, 9.2 x 4.8 cm axially and about 15.8 cm craniocaudally, involving the right psoas major muscle and extending down to the iliac fossa.

clinical_course.event: Empiric piperacillin-tazobactam and albumin infusion were started; first ultrasound-guided aspiration removed 125 ml pus.
Follow-up CT showed persistent perinephric abscess and no size decrease; a 12-French pigtail drain was inserted.
After prolonged piperacillin-tazobactam, albumin, and 18 days of catheter drainage, the patient improved and was discharged.
Two-month CT showed complete absorption of the perinephric abscess.
